title: Capacity budgeting oscillator and HC pricing gates
body:
Purpose: quick working sheet to capture a mid-cycle approach for toggling headcount commitments vs price levers when on-demand token volumes swing.

Summary (one-line): build a small decision oscillator that flips between hiring/contracting and price nudges based on 3-week moving token delta, GPU utilization, and margin headroom.

Context / why now:
- Q3–Q4 cadence shows repeated short-term token surges from one large enterprise trial (regionally concentrated).
- Current slab + burst model leaves us exposed for ~2–3 weeks of high unit cost before we can recruit + provision.
- Need an operational gating structure to avoid knee-jerk price increases while preserving runway.

Key assumptions (work-in-progress):
- Baseline unit-cost per 1k tokens at current mix: $0.42 (weighted).
- Forecast variance window for large-trial churn: +/- 38% token delta week-over-week.
- Time to onboard junior infra capacity (contractor GPU) = 10 working days.
- Time to hire full-time engineer = 45 days.
- Pricing elasticity observed in pilot: ~-0.18 elastic (10% price up => 1.8% drop in usage 2–4w lag).
- Target margin buffer: 22% on hosted API revenue for 90d runway.

High-level oscillator logic (pseudo-steps for runbook):
1) Monitor three signals daily: 3w moving token delta (T), regional GPU utilization (U), and net margin buffer (M).
2) If T > +25% AND U > 78% AND M < 18% => trigger CAPACITY-GREEN (immediate burst pool + contractor hire).
3) If T between +10% and +25% OR U between 65% and 78% => trigger PRICE-COOL (apply targeted 5–8% price nudge to trial cohort, communicate to AE).
4) If T < -15% for 2 consecutive weeks => trigger HC-FREEZE evaluation and consider temporary reassignments.
5) Always run a 72-hour canary after any price change to observe elasticity; revert if usage loss on strategic accounts > 6%.

Headcount curve (rolling 12w lens):
- Core ops hires queued: 3 (SRE x1, Infra Eng x1, Cost Analyst x1) -> ramp dates: Jan/Feb/Mar
- Contractor budget (GPU-backed) allocated up to 120 hrs/week for spike windows; used as 10-day fast ramp.

Pricing sensitivity scenarios (scratch):
Scenario A - Soft nudge: +5% price to trial cohorts only, rollback/hard cap after 72h if upstream churn > 4%. Estimated immediate revenue uplift: +2–3%
Scenario B - Regional lift: +8% in high-util region (EMEA-edge) with targeted credits for strategic accounts. Elasticity risk medium; estimated usage drop 3–5% over 2–3w.
Scenario C - Commitment push: offer 6-month soft-commit with 12% discount vs on-demand; expected to convert 12–18% of trial volume into committed revenue -> reduces burst exposure.

Unit-econ sensitivity table (single-line formula references):
- Base unit cost = infrastructure + cloud egress + amortized infra hires.
- If average batch efficiency improves by 7% (opportunity from Optimize team), unit-cost drops by ~9% -> margin buffer increases materially.

Operational tollgates (what to check before flipping levers):
- Tollgate 1 (Capacity spend): confirm GPU spot pool cost delta vs slab < 1.4x and that burst usage is <= expected 3-week spike volume.
- Tollgate 2 (Customer impact): AE signoff required for price nudge on any account > $100k ARR expected contribution.
- Tollgate 3 (Hiring): Hiring kick-off requires runway check (projected runway post-hire >= 120 days).
- Tollgate 4 (Legal/compliance): Price or SKU changes that affect enterprise contracts must be cleared by legal (JIRA-LEGAL-642).

Action items (owner / ETA):
- Diego: instrument a 3w moving token delta metric and Slack alert (ETA 2026-11-08).
- Priya: build a quick cost delta calculator (sheet) that accepts regional mix and batch-eff. (ETA 2026-11-10).
- Ben: prototype contractor onboarding checklist for 10-day GPU provisioning with vendor contacts. (ETA 2026-11-12).
- Ava: draft AE comms templates for targeted price nudges and canary monitoring plan (ETA 2026-11-09).

Open questions / risks (notes to self):
- How sensitive are strategic enterprise accounts to a targeted price nudge? Need AE qualitative read (schedule 15m with account owners).
- Do we have legal runway to run regional price tests without triggering contract renegotiations? (check master service agreement clauses).
- If we push for commitment offers, what is the ops cost to manage carve-outs and billing changes? (ask Billing eng).

Quick trace links and references:
- Confluence playbook: Capacity orchestration (see linked_artifacts id).
- GitHub: cost-models branch 'oscillator-prototype' (PR linked above).
- Jira: INC-4192 (observability gaps for token delta metric).

Notes on modeling fidelity: this is intentionally low-fidelity for fast ops decisions. We should move any choice that triggers > $75k/month incremental spend into the formal budget spreadsheet and a one-page finance note.

Version history (handy):
- 2026-11-02: initial sketch, raw heuristics.
- 2026-11-05: added sample budget table and sensitivity scenarios.
- 2026-11-11: updated owners, tightened tollgates and added runbook contingencies.

Footnotes: keep this doc as an operational scratchpad. If/when a policy is accepted, create 'capacity-oscillator-operational-runbook' in Confluence and link here.
